body_es: SageMaker Clarify mide el sesgo de un conjunto de datos antes de entrenar comparando cómo se reparten los resultados positivos entre dos grupos demográficos, llamados facet favorecido y facet desfavorecido, y dos de sus métricas de pretraining resumen esa comparación con un solo número. Class Imbalance (CI) mide si un grupo tiene muchas más muestras que el otro en el propio conjunto de datos, con la fórmula (na − nd) / (na + nd), y un valor cercano a cero significa tamaños de muestra equilibrados. Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) mide si la proporción de resultados positivos difiere entre grupos, restando la proporción de aprobados del grupo desfavorecido a la del grupo favorecido; SageMaker Clarify suele usar 0,1 en valor absoluto como referencia habitual para marcar una alerta. El ejemplo calcula ambas métricas a mano sobre solicitudes de préstamo agrupadas por edad, con tasas de aprobación de 70 % para el grupo mayor de 40 años y 40 % para el grupo menor, lo que produce una DPL de 0,3, muy por encima del umbral de referencia. Un error común es corregir el sesgo únicamente rebalanceando las muestras de entrenamiento sin revisar la etiqueta que se está prediciendo: si la etiqueta histórica de aprobado ya arrastra decisiones sesgadas del pasado, un modelo perfectamente balanceado en cantidad de muestras sigue aprendiendo y reproduciendo esa misma disparidad.
body_en: SageMaker Clarify measures bias in a dataset before training by comparing how positive outcomes split between two demographic groups, called the favored facet and the disfavored facet, and two of its pretraining metrics boil that comparison down to a single number. Class Imbalance (CI) measures whether one group has far more samples than the other in the dataset itself, using the formula (na − nd) / (na + nd), with a value near zero meaning balanced sample sizes. Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) measures whether the share of positive outcomes differs between groups, subtracting the disfavored group's approval share from the favored group's; SageMaker Clarify commonly treats an absolute value around 0.1 as the usual reference point for flagging a concern. The example computes both metrics by hand over loan applications grouped by age, with a 70% approval rate for the over-40 group and 40% for the under-40 group, which produces a DPL of 0.3, well past that reference threshold. A common mistake is fixing bias purely by rebalancing how many training samples each group has without reexamining the label being predicted: if the historical approved label already carries biased decisions from the past, a model trained on a perfectly balanced sample count still learns and reproduces that same disparity.
example_code:
def class_imbalance(n_a, n_d):
    return (n_a - n_d) / (n_a + n_d)

def dpl(n_a, n_a_pos, n_d, n_d_pos):
    q_a = n_a_pos / n_a
    q_d = n_d_pos / n_d
    return q_a - q_d

facet_a_total, facet_a_approved = 60, 42  # over_40
facet_d_total, facet_d_approved = 40, 16  # under_40

ci = class_imbalance(facet_a_total, facet_d_total)
gap = dpl(facet_a_total, facet_a_approved, facet_d_total, facet_d_approved)

print(f"Class Imbalance (CI): {round(ci, 3)}")
print(f"Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL): {round(gap, 3)}")
print(f"Approval rate over_40: {round(facet_a_approved / facet_a_total, 3)}")
print(f"Approval rate under_40: {round(facet_d_approved / facet_d_total, 3)}")
if abs(gap) > 0.1:
    print("Flag: pre-training bias above the common 0.1 threshold")
else:
    print("Flag: within the common 0.1 threshold")

Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL): 0.3
Approval rate over_40: 0.7
Approval rate under_40: 0.4

source: AWS Docs — Pre-training Bias Metrics, SageMaker Clarify (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-measure-data-bias.html)
